items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI in Asset Management: Large Language Models, Autonomous Agents and the Information Efficiency of Equity Markets
items.desc: Reviews the empirical literature on language-model sentiment measures in equity markets and proposes an event study of how prices react to AI-based sentiment from earnings calls, asking whether LLMs and autonomous agents improve market information efficiency. [SSRN, posted 2026-11-20]

podcast.speaker: A
podcast.text: Today's paper comes from SSRN, and I should say up front that we're working from the abstract only. It's about artificial intelligence and generative AI in asset management.

podcast.speaker: A
podcast.text: Whether large language models and autonomous agents are making equity markets more informationally efficient. If machines can read earnings calls and filings instantly, prices should absorb news faster.

podcast.speaker: B
podcast.text: So what does the author actually do?

podcast.speaker: A
podcast.text: The paper reviews the existing empirical work on sentiment measures built with language models, and then proposes an event study. The idea is to look at how markets react around earnings calls when an AI-based sentiment signal is available.

podcast.speaker: B
podcast.text: So it's partly a survey and partly a research design.

podcast.speaker: A
podcast.text: Right. Based on the abstract, it frames the proposal rather than reporting a big new headline number, so treat it as a roadmap for testing market efficiency in the age of AI tools.

podcast.speaker: B
podcast.text: Caveat being that a proposed study isn't a finding yet.

podcast.speaker: A
podcast.text: Exactly. Takeaway: a useful map of how researchers might test whether AI sentiment really moves, or sharpens, stock prices.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Welcome to the Daily AI Research Digest for November 28th, 2026. Today is a light day for papers and a busy one for markets and industry news.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Right, Alex. Our one new paper is from SSRN, and the headlines are mostly about AI and Wall Street.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Let's start there. Bloomberg says Washington's message this week was unmistakable: win the AI race with China, with government intervention if needed. That fueled a wild Thanksgiving week.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: And the Wall Street Journal reports the Nasdaq finished its best week since April, as investors took a break from AI jitters.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: But the Financial Times adds a caution. It argues that political meddling around Nvidia has already dulled the dollar and Treasuries, and is now hitting equities too.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: And the FT reports the data centre build-out is adding pressure to defence contractors like Boeing, who already face ballooning backlogs.

briefing.speaker: B

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: On research, a new SSRN paper reviews work on language model sentiment in equity markets and proposes an event study of earnings calls. We're going from the abstract only, so it's a roadmap rather than a result.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Still, it asks the right question: do AI tools make prices more efficient?
